questions.question: What is an armature in the context of 3D skeletal animation?
options: A hierarchy of bones that drives mesh deformation
A set of keyframe data stored in a GLB file
The visible mesh surface of a character
The blend weight between two animation clips
questions.explanation: An armature is the invisible skeleton hierarchy made of bones. It is the structure you animate; the mesh follows it through skinning weight assignments.

questions.question: Why must you pass clock.getDelta() instead of clock.getElapsedTime() to mixer.update()?
options: getElapsedTime() is not available on THREE.Clock
getDelta() returns milliseconds, which Three.js requires
getDelta() returns the time since the last call, keeping playback speed consistent across frames
questions.explanation: getDelta() returns the seconds since it was last called. Passing delta keeps animation speed tied to real time. Passing elapsedTime (a growing total) would make animations run faster and faster.

questions.question: In Mixamo's auto-rig workflow, how many body markers must you place before Mixamo generates the rig?
questions.explanation: Mixamo asks you to place five markers — head top, chin, left and right wrists, groin, and knees — before its AI generates the full ~65-bone rig.

questions.question: Which Three.js class is the playback engine you call update(delta) on every frame?
questions.explanation: AnimationMixer is the playback engine. You create one per animated model and call mixer.update(delta) inside requestAnimationFrame to advance time through the active clips.

questions.question: What method do you call to smoothly blend from one AnimationAction to another over a set duration?
questions.explanation: crossFadeTo is called on the currently playing action. It fades its weight out while fading the target action in over the given duration in seconds.
